chunks: Al-Sakuni narrated from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام, from his father, from his forefathers عليهم السلام, who said:

A man came to Ali عليه السلام and said: Indeed, I have earned wealth, and I was careless in seeking it, [mixing] halal (permissible) and haram (forbidden). I have now intended tawbah (repentance), but I do not know what of it is halal and what is haram, for it has become mixed up for me.

So Ali عليه السلام said: Take out the khums (one-fifth tax) of your wealth, for Allah, Mighty and Exalted, has accepted khums from a person, and the remainder of the wealth, all of it, is halal for you.

key_terms.أَغْمَضْتُ: I was careless or undiscerning in pursuing wealth
key_terms.حَرَامًا: that which is forbidden in earning and ownership
key_terms.حَلَالًا: that which is permissible in earning and ownership
key_terms.خُمُسَ: one-fifth due to be taken from the wealth

ai.seo_question: What should someone do if their wealth contains mixed halal and haram earnings and they cannot distinguish between them?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for one who has acquired wealth through mixed halal and haram means and can no longer distinguish between them, but sincerely seeks tawbah (repentance). Imam Ali عليه السلام instructs him to pay khums, after which the remainder is treated as halal for him.
